text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two Socialist members of the Central Election Commission have told President Sali Berisha he should clarify if he wants to take up an MP's mandate which is not compatible with his presidential duties. The 17-member commission later issued a joint statement saying the letter was not official.
- Albania's foreign ministry staff will be selected on their professional qualities rather than political influences, said Paskal Milo, named to become the next foreign minister.
- The Democratic Party will start a full reconstruction after its resounding election defeat in June 29 to separate its irresponsible part from the responsible part, a senior Democrat said.
- Republican Party chairman Sabri Godo has refused to head a new commission for the compilation of a draft constitution.
- Six people have been killed by firearms in 24 hours in Tirana.
- Two state-owned banks, the Savings Bank and the National Commercial Bank, have registered as commercial holding companies, paving the way for their privatisation.

- Democratic Party Secretary General Genc Pollo will lead the party until autumn when its congress will choose a chairman, a post sought by President Sali Berisha who is about to resign after five years in power.
- The Democratic Party will not attend the first session of parliament.

- Italy and Albania will sign an agreement for cooperation and development. The accord was not signed with the previous Democratic Party government because it refused to shed light on the activity of pyramid schemes.

- Democratic MP Azem Hajdari said Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano, who was sentenced to 12 years in jail for embezzlement, should be deprived of his parliamentary mandate. Nano has declared he will be Albania's next prime minister.
- The Monarchy Party said it does not recognize the results of a nationwide referendum in which two thirds of voters rejected the restoration of the monarchy.
